message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 192, "amount_cents": 3148}, {"order_id": 193, "amount_cents": 9581}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I should check the actual refund and order data rather than trusting W2's summary alone. Starting with list_refunds to verify the applied refunds.
The refunds match W2's report. Next I'll check the orders so I know which customers to pay before calling net_balance.
Refunds match the orders list, and the customers are acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.

Acme's net balance is 33841 cents. The orders and refunds I checked agree with that figure (orders 190 and 193 total 43422, less refund 193 of 9581). I'll record Acme's payout now and then continue with the other customers.
Acme's payout of 33841 is recorded and matches orders 190 and 193 less refund 193. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance is 40664. Orders 191 (26465) and 194 (14199) sum to 40664, and birch has no refunds, so the figure checks out. I'll record Birch's payout now and then fetch Cobalt's balance.
Acme and Birch are paid. The last customer is cobalt, so I'll fetch its net balance from net_balance and check it against orders 192 and 195 less refund 192.

Cobalt's net balance is 18779. Orders 192 (19506) and 195 (2421) sum to 21927, less refund 192 (3148), gives 18779, so the figure checks out. All three customers have been verified, so I'll record Cobalt's payout.
All three payouts are recorded and each matches the order and refund arithmetic I checked: acme 33841, birch 40664, cobalt 18779. The batch is complete.
